metadata.title: Security Context Exception Patterns
metadata.description: Patterns that help separate real security violations from exceptions.

concepts.title: Government
concepts.description: Government authority, ministries, or the governing order.

concepts.title: Terrorism
concepts.description: Promotion, support, glorification, or operational discussion of terrorism.

concepts.title: Public Order
concepts.description: Order, stability, compliance, and societal calm.

entries.title: Documentary Exception
entries.description: Security language that appears in documentary, educational, police, or court contexts.
supporting_evidence: The scene is explicitly framed as reporting or explanation.
The speaker is repeating another person or recording evidence.
contradictory_evidence: The narrator endorses the harmful content.
The story clearly converts the quote into praise.
false_positives: Any mention of terrorism in a documentary report.
A court transcript reproducing a threat as evidence.
counter_examples: A news report on a security incident.
A classroom explanation of security law.
cross_sentence_indicators: The harmful term is introduced in one sentence and explained as evidence in the next.
reviewer_guidance: Do not ignore explicit documentary or court framing.

glossary_relationships.note: Context can explain why the mention is not a violation.

gcam_mappings.note: Use when content is documented rather than endorsed.
